notes: The published fee schedule dates from 2017. Ask for the current cost.

A General Sessions judge sits in probate, and the Clerk and Master clerks that docket. Fees from 01/01/2026: $345.00 for a small estate, a full administration, or muniment of title; $431.40 with creditor notice. Cash, money order, cashier's check or a law firm check only, no cards.
County Clerk, under a population exemption at T.C.A. 18-6-106. The office's own page does not list probate, so confirm by phone. Closed Wednesday and Sunday; open Saturday morning.
Clerk and Master also serves as Clerk of the Probate Court. The county publishes 423-542-1801; an older 423-542-1812 appears nowhere on its page.
E-filing through Tybera, but the original will must be physically delivered.
Probate and Family Court; Clerk and Master is the clerk.
Seventh Circuit Court, Probate Division. The Clerk and Master here does not take probate.

The county's Probate and Juvenile Court was never given jurisdiction over decedents' estates, only over juveniles, so estate filings go to the Clerk and Master. Do not call 615-789-5414, which is the General Sessions clerk.
Probate Court under General Sessions; Clerk and Master is the clerk.
Chancery Court lists open estates among its services, and the County Clerk lists no probate function at all. Fees are not published; call.
Moved from General Sessions to Chancery effective July 1, 2014.
Two offices. Trenton is the county seat; Humboldt is 731-784-9551.
Chancery Part 2. Probate hearings are by appointment only, Tuesday to Friday mornings.
General Sessions; Clerk and Master since 2010.

The Probate and Juvenile Court was repealed effective 2022 and probate returned to chancery. Court offices sit in the Rawlings Building, 102 Thompson Street, though mail goes to the Court Square address.

The County Clerk runs the probate section here, with its own intake form and fee schedule. Small estate $354.50, opening an estate $523.50, or $354.50 with no creditor notice. Open Saturday 8 to 11. Do not call 865-397-2404, which is the Clerk and Master.
Chancery Probate Division, Suite 352, a different counter from Chancery in Suite 125.

This county is mid-transition. Private Acts of 2025 ch. 16 dissolves the Probate and Juvenile Court, but only when the sitting judge's full term expires, and separately permits the county commission to move the probate clerking at any time before that. No published record says whether it has. The 1982 act naming the County Clerk as probate clerk was left unamended and still stands on its face. Call the Clerk and Master at 731-635-1941 and ask whether estate petitions are being received there; if not, the County Clerk is 731-635-2561. Ask which building too, because the 2025 act ordered the court moved to the Justice Complex and three addresses are in circulation.

One officeholder is the Circuit, Criminal, Sessions, Juvenile and Probate Court Clerk. Probate is heard in General Sessions at the Justice Center in Lenoir City, 12680 Highway 11 West, Suite 3. Not the County Clerk and not the Clerk and Master.

Sources conflict and the county publishes nothing that settles it. One set of records puts probate in General Sessions Division II at the Juvenile Court Complex on Irby Street, with its own line at 731-988-3025. Call the Clerk and Master at 731-423-6030 and ask which office takes estate filings and in which building.
The separate Probate Court ceased to exist in 1997.

Probate sits in Chancery. Fees from the schedule effective January 1, 2026: $456.50 to open with publication, $379.50 without, and $379.50 or $384.50 for a small estate. Go between 8:00 and 4:00; the 7:30 to 4:30 figure the county also publishes is staff hours. No e-filing, and a new estate cannot be opened by email or fax.
Probate Court under a General Sessions judge; Clerk and Master since 1990.
A full administration requires an attorney here. The small estate exemption is the carve-out.
The office's own mailing line reads Probate and Juvenile Clerk. 100 E. Court Square, Suite 100, Livingston.
Probate Court under a General Sessions judge; the Circuit Court Clerk is the clerk.

A 1982 act vests probate in General Sessions with the County Clerk as its clerk, and expressly divested the Clerk and Master. The county website is offline and two addresses circulate, so confirm the street address when you call.
General Sessions; the Clerk and Master clerks probate specifically.
Chancery Court, 422 West Court Square, Room 102, Springfield. Open 8:00 to 4:30, Monday to Friday.

General Sessions judges sit as Probate Judge, so filings go to the County Clerk rather than the Clerk and Master. This office runs four locations; probate is a Murfreesboro matter, at 319 N Maple Street. Careful with the county's own filing-fees page: that is the 2016 Chancery schedule and it does not govern probate here, which uses the County Clerk's schedule revised July 1 2018. 615-898-7800 is the number the county publishes. A direct probate line may exist but the county does not publish one, so ask for estates when you call.

Private Acts of 1982 ch. 383 vests all probate jurisdiction in General Sessions and names no clerk for it. Private Acts of 1951 ch. 657 makes the Circuit Court Clerk the clerk of General Sessions, which points one way. T.C.A. 18-6-106 points instead at the Clerk and Master. The county publishes nothing either way and the state's own compilation declines to name a current probate clerk, so both offices are legally defensible. Call the Clerk and Master at 423-663-2627 and the Circuit Court Clerk at 423-663-2440 and ask which one takes estate filings.

Probate is handled in-house by the County Clerk; ask for option 5. IMPORTANT: this county's published probate instructions state that filings must be prepared by a Tennessee-licensed attorney. No Tennessee statute requires counsel, so whether that is a local rule or a strong preference is the first thing to ask on the phone. Fees from 01/01/2026: $433.50 for a small estate, muniment, or probate without publication; $503.50 with publication.
A standing Probate Court with its own elected clerk. Room 124, not the Clerk and Master in Room 308.
Chancery at Blountville specifically, not Kingsport.
No bags or purses clear security. The office moved to the new courthouse on East Main.

An Attorney General opinion issued about this county moved probate clerking off the County Clerk, and the Clerk and Master is where it lands. The County Clerk lists no probate function. Mail goes to PO Box 46, not the general county box. Confirm before filing.
A 1986 act that would have moved probate to the General Sessions clerk was rejected by local voters and never took effect, so probate stayed in chancery. Confirm the street address when you call.
The Clerk and Master's Jonesborough office.
General Sessions; Clerk and Master performs the probate clerk duties.
Electronic filing through Tybera is required. Estates line is 615-591-8538.
General Sessions Division III. Probate is Room 201 on its own line, separate from Chancery.
